newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN EAGER TO END NUERBURGRING BAD LUCK.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN EAGER TO END NUERBURGRING BAD LUCK.

text.p: Unstoppable Australian Michael Doohan hopes to break a long-standing jinx in Sunday's German 500cc Grand Prix.

Three times world champion Doohan, who achieved his seventh success in eight races when he won the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola this month, returns to the Nuerburgring circuit, where he has always been unlucky.

Last year, the Honda rider had to settle for second place behind Italian Luca Cadalora after miscounting the laps. Doohan did not make a last-ditch bid to regain the lead in the final lap because he thought he had another to go.
Two years ago, he raced with a broken finger and tumbled while leading to allow fellow-Australian Darryl Beattie to win.
He also crashed spectacularly in the previous race held at Nuerburgring, in 1990.
Doohan, who has been in a class of his own since the season started, will retain the lead in the world championship standings, whatever happens.

By winning at Imola, the gifted Australian extended his lead to a seemingly invincible 93 points over team mate Alex Criville of Spain, out of action until September since his crash at last month's Dutch Grand Prix.
The main danger for Doohan should come from the Aoki brothers of Japan, both also with Honda.

Nobuatsu Aoki was second to the Australian at Imola and climbed to third in the world championship standings. Younger brother Takuma enjoyed the second podium finish of his career by coming third on the Italian track.
In the 250cc, all eyes will be on local rider Ralf Waldmann, who won here last year on his Honda and has always felt at ease in a race often made tricky by unpredictable weather.
"I like this track, especially when it's wet, and I wouldn't mind a little rain," said German Waldmann, second to Italian rival Max Biaggi in the world championship standings.
World champion Biaggi's victory in a tightly-contested race at Imola took him back on top of the table, five points ahead of Waldmann, who had to be content with fourth place.
In the 125cc category, the man to beat will once again be Italian teenager Valentino Rossi, who has been almost as dominant as Doohan in the races so far.
Aprilia rider Rossi has won six of the season's eight events and heads the championship table by 47 points from Japanese Noboru Ueda.
